1	# Does gate 1's reading give the same answer twice? A repeatability check of the measuring stick (D567's next step), version 3 for the council (rounds 27 to 29)
     2	
     3	**Why.** Gate 1 (Alex's six lines, D400) has been missed in all nine readings, by a few sends a line, with no one fault class
     4	(D557; `carried-run/faults_by_topic.py`). Lines 1 to 3 allow no fault on any written answer choice. Whether a second reading of
     5	the same answer choices, by the same method, names the same faults has never been measured (searched D396 to D567; Stage B had
     6	`stage_b/line_chance.py`, Stage A none). This check measures that: how much of each line's verdict and of its failing sends
     7	changes when the identical sends are read again. It does not establish which reading is right, does not apportion the nine
     8	misses between the step and the reading, and changes no line (council round 27).
     9	
    10	**The re-reading.** The fortnight's gate-1 reading (`poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/`, 39 sends) is read again from
    11	the start by the unchanged tooling and the unchanged briefs, in a new folder: the same packets (`build_reader_packets.py`, same
    12	seed), two fresh first-reader sessions of each family, the disputes and named W faults sent to two fresh third readers, one of
    13	each family (`collect_readings.py disputes`, `ladder/stage-a-third-reader-brief.md`), and the report with both treatments of
    14	unresolved points (`collect_readings.py report`). The first reading's files are copied, never edited.
    15	
    16	**Controls** (`controls.json`, frozen before any re-reading; checked by Claude against the article and the brief:
    17	author-checked, not independent; reported, deciding nothing): three sends whose fault Claude confirms (Q: `c1/clean-1` pass 3, the
    18	question leans on an unnamed lab; R: `c1/clean-7` pass 1, "and" in the question against "or" in the Yes rung; L: `c1/clean-13` pass
    19	1, two of the thesis's checkpoints neither asked nor listed as not judged) and three sends Claude reads as sound on Q, L and R
    20	(`c1/clean-5` pass 1, `c1/clean-9` pass 2, `c1/clean-11` pass 3). The fresh readers see the same items as before, with no mark of
    21	the first reading and no sign of which items are controls.
    22	
    23	**The comparison** (`compare_readings.py`, written and tested before the re-reading on a copy altered in known ways: a new fault
    24	appears as "second only", a removed one as "first only", a missing ruling makes the reading "not measured" and stops the comparison
    25	of its sends; `compare-selftest.txt`). It runs the gate's own accounting (`accounting.account`, as `collect_readings.py report`)
    26	on each reading under each treatment of unresolved points and reports, without a conclusion of its own: each line's verdict in
    27	each reading, "not measured" kept apart from met and missed; for lines 1 to 3 the failing sends in both readings, in the first
    28	only and in the second only, each with its size and the union's (an empty union said so); per send the Q, L and R values that
    29	changed; the W faults upheld in each reading with their reasons; the topics right under line 5; the dispute shares; the controls
    30	against each reading.
    31	
    32	**What is said afterwards:** what the comparison shows, in those terms (the two readings agreed or differed on a line's verdict;
    33	how many failing sends recurred, against each denominator). Nothing is concluded about which reading is right or about how much of
    34	the nine misses the reading caused; no probability is computed.
    35	
    36	**Limits.** One re-reading of one fortnight (39 sends, 13 topics, related sends); the same two model families, whose standards
    37	recur, and the same packets in the same order, so shared order effects can make agreement look stronger; the briefs as used. Reader sessions are outside every ledger ($0).

item.text:
**No-go until the comparison refuses a missing third-reader family.** The script falls back to one third reader when it finds only one family’s files. That can produce a “complete” reading even though this design requires two families and both unresolved treatments. A missing family must make the comparison incomplete, not silently change its method. [compare_readings.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/compare_readings.py:23)

Two smaller checks should be completed before the reading:

- The saved [compare-selftest.txt](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/compare-selftest.txt) shows the new and removed faults, but does **not** show the claimed missing-ruling test. Save that result, and add a check in which an entire third-reader family is absent.
- The design promises the **topics** right under line 5, while the comparison prints the accounting’s counts, not the topic identities. Either add those identities or narrow the design’s promise. Verify the two folders contain the same 39 outcomes before comparing them. [DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/DESIGN.md:23), [comparison code](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/gate1-stick/compare_readings.py:74)

The revised interpretation is sound: it reports changes without assigning truth or a probability, and it states the limits of repeating the same packets with the same families. The author-checked controls are correctly labelled and do not decide the outcome.

CONSENSUS: no, because a missing third-reader family can silently become a one-reader ruling, and the promised comparison checks are not all evidenced.
